The pus was sent for Gram stain, culture, acid-fast bacilli (AFB) stain and histopathological evaluation. The pituitary was not removed.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old Bahraini man presented in March 2016 with a one-month history of severe continuous headache exacerbated by bright light, photosensitivity, nausea, left eye blurred vision, and generalized fatigue. He reported symptoms of hypopituitarism including loss of libido, erectile dysfunction, polyuria, and polydipsia. MRI brain revealed a heterogeneously hyperintense T2-weighted sellar/suprasellar lesion with peripheral hypointensity not suppressed on FLAIR, fluid level on T1, and mass effect compressing the optic chiasm and cavernous sinuses. Endocrine assessment confirmed central hypogonadism, central hypoadrenalism, and mildly elevated prolactin with normal thyroid function. In July 2016, transsphenoidal surgery was performed, revealing a thick-walled abscess containing yellowish pus that was drained; the pituitary gland was preserved. Histopathology confirmed an inflammatory lesion consistent with abscess and excluded pituitary adenoma. Gram stain showed few WBC with sterile culture, and AFB stain was negative. Postoperatively, the patient received broad-spectrum antibiotics (metronidazole, ceftriaxone, and vancomycin) for 6 weeks, with clinical improvement and return to normal functional status. Follow-up MRI demonstrated complete resolution with no enhancing residual abscess pockets.
